primary_meaning: In mainstream Christian teaching, 'the heart of the earth' (Matthew 12:40) is understood as a reference to Jesus' burial in the tomb/grave — and, in much traditional interpretation, his sojourn in the realm of the dead (Sheol/Hades) — during the interval between his death and resurrection. It functions as the antitype of Jonah's three days and nights in the belly of the great fish, serving as the 'sign of Jonah' that prefigures Christ's death, burial, and resurrection on the third day.
primary_basis: Matthew 12:40 (the primary text: 'as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth')
Jonah 1:17 and Jonah 2:2 (Jonah in the fish's belly, crying 'out of the belly of Sheol')
Psalm 16:10 with Acts 2:24-31 (his soul not abandoned to Sheol/Hades; his flesh not seeing corruption)
Ephesians 4:9 ('he descended into the lower parts of the earth,' often read in parallel)
1 Peter 3:18-19 (proclamation to the spirits in prison, cited in the descent-to-Hades tradition)
Matthew 27:57-60; Mark 15:46 (the burial narratives supplying the referent of the tomb)

alternatives.meaning: The tomb/grave only — a strictly physical reading in which 'heart of the earth' means burial in the ground, without any conscious descent into an underworld realm; common among interpreters who reject or minimize the 'descent into hell' doctrine.
basis: 1 Corinthians 15:3-4 ('buried... raised on the third day')

alternatives.meaning: Sheol/Hades as a distinct underworld realm — emphasizing Christ's active descent to the place of the dead (the 'harrowing of hell' in patristic, Catholic, Orthodox, and some Protestant tradition), not merely the tomb.
basis: Apostles' Creed ('he descended into hell/to the dead') as a traditional interpretive anchor

alternatives.meaning: Jerusalem or the 'heart' of the land/world — a minority reading (advanced by some who count the three days and nights from Jesus' arrest or betrayal rather than burial) taking 'earth' as the land or the city at its center, so the period includes Gethsemane and the trials.
basis: Ezekiel 5:5 (Jerusalem 'in the midst of the nations')
Matthew 26:45-56 (delivery into the hands of men as the starting point)

alternatives.meaning: 'Heart of the earth' as the grip/power of sinful men or the world-system — a rare figurative reading in which Jesus is 'in the heart of the earth' from the moment he is handed over to human power.
basis: Matthew 17:22 ('the Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men')

notes: The phrase occurs only once in Scripture (Matthew 12:40). There is broad, recognizable consensus that it refers to Christ's death-and-burial interval prior to resurrection; the live disagreements concern (a) whether it denotes the tomb alone or also Hades/Sheol, and (b) the chronology (how to reconcile 'three days and three nights' with a Friday burial and Sunday resurrection — a debate that fuels Wednesday/Thursday-crucifixion proposals and the minority 'Jerusalem/arrest' reading). These are debates within a settled core meaning rather than rival core meanings.
